Nov 10 (Reuters) - Mercor said on Tuesday it had raised $750 million in a funding round that valued the AI training startup at $20 billion.
The Series D round drew participation from Benchmark, Felicis, Fundomo, Nvidia and funds managed by affiliates of Apollo, among others.
Here are more details:
• Investor enthusiasm for AI has fueled a sharp rise in private funding this year, creating a growing group of heavily capitalized startups carrying multibillion-dollar valuations
• Mercor, which began as an AI-powered hiring platform, now connects technology companies with subject-matter experts whose knowledge is used to train, test and improve AI models and agents
• The San Francisco-based company said it will use the funding to help train and test AI agents on professional tasks
• "Every job in the economy will need its own AI agents and every company will need a way to train and evaluate them on its own work," co-CEO Brendan Foody said
• According to Crunchbase, AI-driven startups raised $102 billion, or 64% of global venture capital, in the third quarter of 2026
• Mercor, which is backed by Jack Dorsey and venture capitalist Peter Thiel, was valued at about $10 billion after raising $350 million in October last year
(Reporting by Pragyan Kalita in Bengaluru; Editing by Shreya Biswas)

Capital Influx Amid Scaling Demands
OpenAI has successfully secured $15 billion in fresh funding, bringing the artificial intelligence leader to a $1.25 trillion valuation. This capital injection arrives as the company accelerates its massive infrastructure build-out, which requires significant spending on data centers and high-performance computing hardware. Recent reports indicate that Nvidia has contributed approximately $30 billion to OpenAI , while SoftBank has provided roughly $65 billion.
Financial Metrics and Market Context
The latest financing round represents half of the $30 billion target OpenAI originally sought. The valuation reflects a 47% increase over the $852 billion post-money valuation recorded in March 2026. Despite a 50% revenue growth between the second and third quarters, the firm remains heavily reliant on external capital to sustain its operations.
Anthropic is preparing for a public market debut on the Nasdaq as early as November 19.
Anthropic valuation in the upcoming IPO is expected to range between $1.2 trillion and $1.3 trillion.
Private placement commitments from investors including Google , Microsoft , and AMD total $26 billion for the Anthropic listing.
The proximity of these two major funding events highlights the extreme capital intensity of the generative AI sector. Investors are now closely watching the public markets to determine if Anthropic will command a premium over the valuations currently seen in private funding rounds.
Timing is critical. The market is shifting. Investors are demanding clearer paths to profitability as development costs mount. For OpenAI and its peers, the race for infrastructure dominance continues unabated.

Norwest: $4 Billion Fund Expands Global Multi-Stage Investment Strategy
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 11:42 AM
Norwest: $4 Billion Fund Expands Global Multi-Stage Investment Strategy
Norwest has closed Norwest 18, a $4 billion global investment fund that will back venture and growth equity opportunities across technology, healthcare, and consumer markets. The vehicle is the largest fund in the firm’s 65-year history and increases its total capital under management to $18 billion.
Norwest will deploy the new fund across the United States, India, and Israel, continuing a strategy that spans early-stage venture investments through later-stage growth equity. The firm said this flexible approach allows it to begin working with companies at different stages and continue supporting them as their capital requirements and operating priorities evolve.
Since launching Norwest 17 in April 2024, the firm has completed more than 87 investments and worked with over 30 portfolio companies on liquidity events. Initial public offerings during that period included Amagi Media Labs, BillionToOne, MBX Biosciences, Omada Health, and Swiggy.
Strategic acquisitions involving Norwest-backed businesses included EQT’s acquisition of Avetta, Luminate Capital Partners’ purchase of AbsenceSoft, Gilead Sciences’ acquisition of Ouro Medicines, Salesforce’s purchase of Qualified, Pinterest’s acquisition of tvScientific, and ServiceNow’s purchase of Veza.
Norwest 18 will maintain the firm’s primary sector focus while increasing its exposure to emerging categories. Areas of interest include next-generation financial infrastructure, physical and voice AI, agentic cybersecurity, technology-enabled industrial and aerospace businesses, and healthcare AI.
Recent financial infrastructure investments include Beltic, Rain, and Stablecore. Norwest has also backed Coval, Generalist AI, and LlamaIndex in intelligent AI systems; Above Security, ORION Security, Red Access, and Zenity in cybersecurity; and East Range Group, Padmini VNA, JJG Aerospace, and Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group in industrial and aerospace markets.
Healthcare investments include Infinx, Matchpoint Therapeutics, Rezo Therapeutics, Tokaido Health, and Vitalize Care. These businesses are applying AI to drug discovery, clinical and administrative workflows, healthcare access, and care-team productivity.
Beyond financing, Norwest provides portfolio companies with operating support and strategic guidance. The firm has doubled the size of its Senior Advisor Network, added operating executives, and launched the Norwest Operator Collective and Norwest Kinetic. These resources are intended to help management teams address technology, go-to-market, talent, and organizational challenges.
Since its founding in 1961, Norwest has invested in more than 750 companies and currently works with over 275 venture and growth equity portfolio companies. Its offices are in Menlo Park, San Francisco, Mumbai, and Tel Aviv.
KEY QUOTES
“Building and scaling a company has never been a linear journey, and today that journey is becoming more complex. Companies are staying private longer, scaling across markets, and navigating critical decisions around technology, talent, and growth. Capital is only one part of what they need. Our role is to be a long-term partner and bring the experience, networks, and resources that can help leadership teams make those decisions with confidence.”
Jeff Crowe, Senior Managing Partner at Norwest
“Markets and technology change, but what has remained consistent at Norwest is our ability to identify strong businesses, invest patiently, and stay closely aligned with the founders, CEOs, and leadership teams we partner with. Our multi-stage strategy allows us to meet companies where they are and continue supporting them as they grow. Norwest 18 gives us even greater flexibility to do that across sectors, stages, and geographies.”
Jon Kossow, Managing Partner at Norwest

candidates.text:
Pfizer: Up To $1.5 Billion Funding Agreement With Blackstone Life Sciences To Advance Monthly GLP-1 Obesity Drug
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 2:21 PM
Pfizer: Up To $1.5 Billion Funding Agreement With Blackstone Life Sciences To Advance Monthly GLP-1 Obesity Drug
Pfizer and Blackstone Life Sciences have entered into a strategic funding agreement under which funds managed by Blackstone will provide up to $1.5 billion through 2028 to support the clinical development of berobenatide, Pfizer’s investigational monthly GLP-1 receptor agonist for chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions.
The agreement will help Pfizer advance its obesity drug development program while maintaining financial flexibility to invest in other therapeutic areas. In exchange for its funding commitment, Blackstone will become eligible for milestone-based payments tied to U.S. regulatory approval and commercial performance.
Berobenatide is being developed as a potential first-in-class monthly injectable GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide. Pfizer is evaluating the treatment for chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions, including knee osteoarthritis and obstructive sleep apnea.
The transaction represents a significant investment in Pfizer’s cardiometabolic pipeline as the pharmaceutical company advances a broad portfolio of investigational obesity therapies.
How The $1.5 Billion Funding Agreement Works
Under the agreement, Blackstone-managed funds will cover up to $1.5 billion in development expenses associated with berobenatide through 2028.
In return, Blackstone will be eligible to receive payments if the drug achieves specified regulatory and commercial milestones.
These payments are contingent on U.S. regulatory approval of monthly injectable berobenatide monotherapy for chronic weight management and the achievement of certain sales targets.
Any milestone payments earned by Blackstone would be distributed over multiple years.
The structure allows Pfizer to obtain external funding for a major clinical development program without selling ownership or commercial rights to the investigational medicine.
Pfizer will retain full operational control and decision-making authority over berobenatide, including its clinical development strategy.
The agreement also does not provide Blackstone with an ownership interest in the drug.
Funds managed by Blackstone’s perpetual private equity strategy, BXPE, will participate alongside funds managed by Blackstone Life Sciences.
The arrangement illustrates an alternative approach to financing pharmaceutical research, in which investment firms provide capital to support clinical development in exchange for payments linked to future milestones.
For Pfizer, the agreement provides an opportunity to share development costs while retaining control over a potentially important pipeline asset.
Berobenatide Targets Monthly GLP-1 Treatment
Berobenatide is an investigational GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide being studied for chronic weight management and related medical conditions.
GLP-1 receptor agonists act on biological pathways involved in appetite regulation, blood glucose control, and other metabolic processes.
Existing treatments in this drug class have established a significant market for obesity and metabolic disease therapies.
Pfizer is developing berobenatide as a potential monthly injectable treatment, which could offer a different administration schedule from therapies requiring more frequent dosing.
The company is pursuing an extensive clinical development program to evaluate the drug’s safety and effectiveness.
Pfizer plans to advance more than 20 clinical trials involving obesity and associated medical conditions during 2026.
These include 10 ongoing and planned Phase 3 trials for berobenatide.
The studies are intended to evaluate the treatment across chronic weight management and obesity-related conditions.
Pfizer is also investigating berobenatide in combination with other investigational therapies.
The company is studying combinations involving nutrient-stimulated hormone peptides, including amylin analogs.
These approaches are part of Pfizer’s broader strategy to develop treatments that act on multiple biological pathways associated with weight regulation and metabolic health.
Berobenatide remains investigational, and its safety, effectiveness, and potential approval have not yet been established by regulators.
Expanding Pfizer’s Cardiometabolic Pipeline
Pfizer is positioning berobenatide as a central component of its cardiometabolic research and development portfolio.
The company is evaluating the therapy both as a standalone treatment and in combination with other investigational medicines.
Its development strategy extends beyond weight loss to conditions associated with obesity.
Knee osteoarthritis and obstructive sleep apnea are among the conditions included in the clinical research program.
Obesity can contribute to a range of medical complications, creating opportunities for therapies that improve weight management and potentially address related health outcomes.
Pfizer’s clinical program is intended to generate evidence about berobenatide’s potential across different patient populations and treatment settings.
The agreement with Blackstone provides additional resources to support this work through 2028.
Pfizer said the funding arrangement will also allow it to maintain capacity for investment across its broader pharmaceutical pipeline.
By supplementing internal research spending with external capital, the company aims to pursue multiple development priorities simultaneously.
Blackstone Life Sciences Expands Its Pharmaceutical Financing Partnerships

Whitecap Resources raises 2026 production guidance and dividend after posting record Q3 funds flow of $1.2 billion
By Kelly Lippke · November 15, 2026 · 8:45 AM · 5 min read
Written by Kelly Lippke
Calgary-based Whitecap Resources (TSX: WCP) posted Q3 2026 funds flow of $888 million USD (CAD 1.2 billion) — a company record, and a 32% per-share jump from the same quarter a year ago . Production averaged 390,720 boe/d, beating internal forecasts for the period.
Off the back of those results, Whitecap’s board raised full-year 2026 production guidance to 392,000 boe/d — the third upward revision of the year. They also bumped the monthly dividend about 1.5% to $0.046 USD ($0.0617 CAD) per share and approved a 2027 capital budget of $1.78–$1.92 billion USD (CAD 2.4–2.6 billion), targeting average output of 400,000–410,000 boe/d.
Q3 2026 production and financial results
Whitecap’s Q3 2026 output of 390,720 boe/d — 61% liquids — cleared internal forecasts and improved on the 374,623 boe/d from Q3 2025. Funds flow hit $866 million USD (CAD 1.17 billion) , or $0.71 USD ($0.96 CAD) per diluted share, a 32% per-share increase year-over-year. The headline number was strong, and the underlying details held up just as well.
The board raised the monthly dividend about 1.5% to $0.046 USD ($0.0617 CAD) per share, or $0.55 USD ($0.74 CAD) annualized, starting with the November 2026 payment.
Free funds flow reached $474 million USD (CAD 640 million) after $394 million USD (CAD 533 million) in capital expenditures. Through the first nine months of 2026, free funds flow totaled $1.41 billion USD (CAD 1.9 billion) — a solid cash generation pace for a company actively investing in growth.
Net income came in at $241 million USD (CAD 326 million), or $0.20 USD ($0.27 CAD) per share. A non-cash unrealized loss of roughly $222 million USD (CAD 300 million) on commodity contracts — driven by rising forward prices during the quarter — held that figure back. Stripping out that accounting item leaves an even cleaner underlying operating picture.
Drivers behind the outperformance
Several factors pushed production above forecast. Strong base and new well performance at Gold Creek and Kaybob Duvernay, combined with solid output from the Conventional division, moved volumes above plan. Higher light oil and condensate prices lifted realized revenues significantly — crude oil and condensate averaged $84.28 USD ($113.89 CAD) per barrel in Q3 2026, compared to $62.41 USD ($84.34 CAD) per barrel in Q3 2025.
Faster capital cycle times allowed Whitecap to run its drilling program ahead of schedule , and that efficiency showed up directly in per-boe operating costs: $7.56 USD ($10.22 CAD) in Q3 2026, down from $8.79 USD ($11.88 CAD) in Q2 2026. The company also commissioned the Lator 04-13 battery in early Q4 2026 — slightly ahead of schedule and within budget — securing a useful operational win heading into 2027. Related

Updated 2026 guidance, dividend increase, and balance sheet
With Q3 momentum behind it, Whitecap raised full-year 2026 production guidance to 392,000 boe/d — the third upward revision of the year. That implied Q4 output of 395,000 to 400,000 boe/d. To support that pace, the company increased its 2026 capital budget by about $74 million USD (CAD 100 million) to roughly $1.63 billion USD (CAD 2.2 billion), with incremental activity focused on Kaybob, Lator, and Saskatchewan light oil assets.
The board raised the monthly dividend about 1.5% to $0.046 USD ($0.0617 CAD) per share, or $0.55 USD ($0.74 CAD) annualized, starting with the November 2026 payment. The increase added around $9.6 million USD (CAD 13 million) per year in dividend costs — modest, but a clear signal of confidence in the cash flow outlook .
The balance sheet improved substantially over the first nine months of 2026. Net debt fell by about $962 million USD (CAD 1.3 billion) since year-end 2025 to $1.55 billion USD (CAD 2.1 billion), putting the net debt-to-annualized funds flow ratio at 0.4 times. Whitecap’s undrawn $1.85 billion USD (CAD 2.5 billion) credit facility remains fully available, providing genuine financial flexibility heading into 2027.
2027 capital budget and production targets
The board approved a 2027 capital budget of $1.78 to $1.92 billion USD (CAD 2.4 to 2.6 billion), targeting average production of 400,000 to 410,000 boe/d at 60% liquids. On a per-share basis, that works out to roughly 3% annual production growth — or about 5% excluding a planned major turnaround at the Kaybob 15-07 gas plant in Q3 2027, which is expected to shave around 8,000 boe/d off the annual average .
The program includes drilling 127 Unconventional (Montney and Duvernay) wells and 205 Conventional wells, with about 75% of capital going to the Unconventional division. That segment is forecast to average roughly 265,000 boe/d in 2027 — up about 8% from 2026 — led by the Lator ramp-up and Kaybob capacity expansion to 135,000–140,000 boe/d by year-end 2027.
At US$80 per barrel WTI, Whitecap forecasts 2027 funds flow of about $3.03 billion USD (CAD 4.1 billion), generating around $1.18 billion USD (CAD 1.6 billion) in free funds flow after capital spending . That serves as the base case before any potential policy-driven uplift. Related

Databento raised $100 million in a Series C round that values the market data platform at $1.1 billion. The company, which employs 39 people, counts five of the six largest frontier AI labs among its enterprise customers.
Databento, a market data platform serving the financial industry, raised $100 million in a Series C round that values the company at $1.1 billion.
Fifth Down Capital, which first backed Databento before it generated revenue, led the round. Most existing investors returned, including NEA, DRW Venture Capital, Tribe Capital and Hedosophia. Fitch Ventures joined as a strategic investor, bringing the perspective of a large financial information business with experience in credit ratings, financial data and market analysis.
The round closed months after a $97 million Series B. Since that earlier deal, Databento more than doubled its revenue and stayed profitable.
Databento's customers include quantitative trading firms, brokerages, asset managers, commodities businesses and digital asset firms. The company also holds enterprise agreements with five of the six largest frontier AI labs.
The company employed 39 people when the Series C closed. It reached the $1.1 billion valuation with a workforce smaller than those of conventional market data vendors.
"In this AI era, we're seeing remarkably small teams build billion-dollar companies, but that level of efficiency is unprecedented in the market data industry. Until now, reaching this milestone required hundreds of employees given the sheer scale of physical infrastructure involved. I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished, and we'll continue to prioritize exceptional talent as we grow," Christina Qi, co-founder and CEO, said.
"Fifth Down first invested in Databento pre-revenue, as we recognized early on that the company had an opportunity to challenge the established model for delivering financial market data. Our confidence has only grown as Databento's traction and execution have demonstrated it can serve demanding institutional customers, sustain rapid growth, and build a profitable business. Databento's performance has reinforced our original thesis and strengthened our conviction in the company. We are thankful to Christina and Luca for the opportunity to increase our investment and involvement by leading the Series C financing," Andrew Spellman, founder and CEO of Fifth Down Capital, said.
Databento plans to spend the new capital on its market data infrastructure and on expanding coverage into more asset classes. The platform delivers live and historical data for futures, options, equities and indices through a single API. Because it controls each layer of its technology, from the original data source to final delivery, Databento says it is the first service of its kind to combine the speed and reliability that top trading firms require with a simpler experience for developers.

Ex-Anthropic researchers' startup Mirendil raises $1 billion to let AI agents do the work of an AI lab
Nov 13, 2026
·
7:07 PM

By MLQ.ai Newsroom · Edited by Peter Foy
·
4 min read
Key points
Mirendil raised a $1 billion Series A led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital, with Battery Ventures, Doerr Capital, Gil & Co, Google, M13, Pear VC and S32 also investing; it did not disclose a valuation [1] .
The round follows a $200 million seed in June at a $1 billion valuation, co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins with Nvidia joining [5] ; reports in September said Mirendil was seeking up to $1 billion at a $5 billion valuation [6] .
Mirendil says one researcher working with agents pretrained its Mirendil-Base coding model from scratch in 3.5 months for less than $10 million in all-in compute, with agents writing more than 99% of the code [2] .
Its products are Fern, a model with a context window of up to 10 million tokens, and Lor, a private-beta platform that runs hundreds of agents writing code and running experiments for days [1] [3] [4] .
Mirendil, a startup founded by two former Anthropic researchers to automate the work of building AI, has raised $1 billion in a Series A round led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital, the company said on Thursday, Nov. 12 [1] . Battery Ventures, Doerr Capital, Gil & Co, Google , M13, Pear VC and S32 also invested, along with other new and existing investors. Mirendil did not disclose its valuation [1] .
The round comes five months after a $200 million seed at a $1 billion valuation, which Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins co-led and Nvidia joined [5] . In September, reports said the company was in talks to raise up to $1 billion at a $5 billion valuation with Kleiner Perkins leading [6] ; Mirendil's announcement confirms the size and the lead but not the price.
One researcher, 3.5 months, under $10 million
Mirendil's pitch is that agents can now do most of the hands-on work of an AI lab, so a small team can build what used to take an institution. "When agents do the hands-on work, the size of your team stops limiting what you can build," the company wrote [1] .
Its main evidence is Mirendil-Base, a coding model it published results for on Oct. 21. Mirendil says a single researcher, working with agents, pretrained it from scratch in 3.5 months with less than $10 million in compute, a figure it describes as all-in, including the agents' token spend, data processing and every small-scale experiment [2] . Agents wrote more than 99% of the code, ran experiments and diagnosed failures, while the researcher decided what to try and what to trust; the company says it used only publicly available data, no distillation and no licensed datasets [2] . These are Mirendil's own figures and have not been independently replicated.
Mirendil then post-trained the base model into Fern, which it says can hold up to 10 million tokens in context, about half a million lines of code or days of an agent's work at once [3] . Fern 0.1 is listed at 0.1 to 0.5 trillion parameters, with access "coming soon"; larger Mirendil-Base-Large and Mirendil-Base-XL models, at up to 2 trillion and 10 trillion parameters, are still in pretraining [3] . The company corrected two figures in its Fern post on Oct. 27 to "more accurately reflect" its training results [3] .
Lor, the product it plans to sell
Lor, in private beta, is the platform Mirendil uses internally and wants to sell. It runs hundreds of agents at a time that write code, run experiments and iterate for days, provision their own GPUs and split jobs across dozens of sub-agents [4] . It works with outside frontier models, including Anthropic's Claude Opus and Claude Fable, OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra, and open models such as Kimi, DeepSeek and GLM, as well as Mirendil's own [4] . In one example, 102 agents built training environments from 100 PyTorch pull requests in an average of eight minutes each [4] .
Neyshabur, the chief executive, and Mehta met at Google in 2019, moved to Anthropic in late 2024 and left in December 2025 [5] . Neyshabur spent more than five years at Alphabet co-leading reasoning research for Gemini, and Mehta built the first version of Anthropic's internal AI-research platform [5] . Mirendil launched with about 20 researchers and engineers from Anthropic, xAI, Google DeepMind and OpenAI [7] , and it still calls itself "a small team" [1] .
The company frames its goal as handing frontier AI research to scientists and engineers outside the big labs [1] . That puts it in the most contested part of AI development: Anthropic has described recursive self-improvement, in which AI systems speed up their own development, as a potential danger, while Mirendil's founders call it the shortest path to faster science and a risk that can be supervised [5] . Thinking Machines Lab is chasing a related market; last week it released Inkling 2 Small, a model built to run AI training jobs ( our story ).

This is a weekly feature that runs down the week’s Top 10 announced funding rounds in the U.S. Check out last week’s biggest funding deal roundup here .
It was another big week for AI-related startup financings. Mirendil , a developer of agentic AI for R&D, led the pack with a $1 billion series A, followed by Mercor , which secured $750 million to connect AI developers with human experts.
Overall, the vast majority of this week’s largest rounds were AI-related, though we did see some biotech, fintech and enterprise software in the mix.
1. Mirendil , $1B, AI for R&D: Mirendil, a developer of agentic AI technology for research and development, secured $1 billion in a Series A funding. Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital led the round for the San Francisco-based startup.
2. Mercor , $750M, human-led AI training: Mercor, a platform that connects AI developers with human experts for model training and evaluation, raised $750 million in Series D funding. The round, backed by a long list of venture investors, set a $20 billion valuation for the San Francisco-based company, which was founded less than four years ago.
3. Torus , $500M, AI infrastructure: Salt Lake City-based Torus, a manufacturer of distributed power and compute infrastructure, announced a $500 million growth financing led by Magnetar Capital . It also introduced a product called Foundry, described as modular AI infrastructure for inference compute.
4. (tied) Path Robotics , $300M, AI for manufacturing: Path Robotics, a developer of physical AI technology for robotics and manufacturing, with initial expertise in welding, picked up $300 million in Series E financing. Georgian led the round, which set a $2.45 billion valuation for the Columbus, Ohio-based company.
4. (tied) LangChain , $300M, agentic AI: LangChain, developer of a platform to run, improve and govern AI agents, closed on $300 million in Series C funding at a $3 billion valuation. CapitalG led the round for the 4-year-old, San Francisco-based company.
6. Nominal , $240M, hardware engineering tools: Nominal, a developer of intelligence tools for hardware engineering, raised $240 million at a $3 billion valuation. Lightspeed Venture Partners and Insight Partners led the round for the Austin-based startup.
7. (tied) Imprint , $130M, fintech: Imprint, a payments, loyalty and customer intelligence platform for brands, landed $130 million in new funding at a $1.9 billion valuation. Khosla Ventures led the financing for the 6-year-old, New York-based company.
7. (tied) Mavria , $130M, AI infrastructure: Mavria, a startup focused on standardizing how AI infrastructure is developed, built and deployed, launched publicly and said it has raised $130 million in pre-seed and seed funding to date. Its latest round, led by Paradigm , sets a $1 billion valuation for the startup, whose founders formerly worked at the U.S. Department of Energy .
9. (tied) Delix Therapeutics , $100M, biotech: Delix Therapeutics, a startup that says it has “reverse-engineered and optimized psychedelics” to develop treatments for psychiatric and psychological disorders, closed on $100 million in Series C funding. Johnson & Johnson Innovation and SV Health Investors ’ Dementia Discovery Fund led the financing for the Bedford, Massachusetts-based company.
9. (tied) Rox , $100M, sales automation: San Francisco-based Rox, developer of an AI revenue agent for enterprise sales, announced a $100 million Series B financing led by General Catalyst and March Capital .
9. (tied) Databento , $100M, financial market data: Databento, a finance data platform, secured $100 million in Series C funding at a $1.1 billion valuation. Fifth Down Capital led the round for the Salt Lake City-based company.

AEVEX Raises 2026 Revenue to $840 Million with Drone Growth
Published on: 14 November، 2026
AEVEX
AEVEX raised its revenue expectations to $840 million in 2026, with growing demand for drones and the expansion of autonomous marine systems.
American uncrewed defense systems company AEVEX has raised its 2026 revenue expectations to $840 million, after recording a 56.5% year-over-year growth in third-quarter revenue, signaling expanding military demand for drones and autonomous systems alongside the company’s expansion into maritime fields.
The company announced revenue of $189.7 million during the third quarter, compared to $121.2 million in the same period of 2025, while adjusted EBITDA rose to $30.8 million, compared to $17.8 million.
AEVEX raised its annual revenue guidance range to $820–$840 million, compared to $700–$720 million previously, and also increased its adjusted EBITDA guidance to $128–$132 million.
Growth Beyond Reliance on Ukraine Programs
One of the most significant shifts in AEVEX’s results is the growth of its core business outside of Ukraine programs, reflecting a broadening customer base and U.S. military orders.
Management stated that core revenue, excluding the Phoenix Ghost and EUCOM Deep Strike programs, reached $137 million in the third quarter, compared to $49 million in the first quarter of the year; new orders for core business also rose to $250.2 million during the third quarter, compared to $65.8 million in the first quarter, reflecting accelerating demand for the company’s systems.
According to management, core revenue surpassed Ukraine-related revenue for the first time since the second quarter of 2025 during the third quarter, marking an important shift toward a more diversified revenue base; the company expects Ukraine revenue of about $36.3 million in the fourth quarter before such revenue declines later, while targeting core revenue between $440 million and $460 million during 2026.
$400 Million Contract… But Actual Value Tied to Orders
AEVEX announced a multi-year U.S. contract with a ceiling value of approximately $400 million to supply uncrewed aircraft systems and related services. The contract represents a flexible framework allowing the customer to issue orders according to operational needs, but it does not mean the entire value has been funded or converted into confirmed revenue.
Management stated that it expects orders related to the contract to be issued during the upcoming period, with potential timing delays due to contractual procedures, but it views the agreement as bolstering revenue opportunities through 2027. The deal derives its importance from reflecting the shift in military demand toward systems that can be manufactured in large quantities and adapted to various mission requirements, rather than relying on fixed-use platforms.
BlackSea Expands AEVEX from Air to Sea
AEVEX’s acquisition of BlackSea Technologies represents one of the most prominent strategic shifts for the company during 2026, adding the marine systems sector to its portfolio and expanding its scope of activity from drones to surface and subsurface systems.
AEVEX expects the Maritime Systems sector to generate revenue of approximately $150 million during 2026, with continued growth the following year. The company relies on integrating autonomy, command, control, and mission planning technologies across its various platforms, allowing for the development of systems capable of operating in a more coordinated manner across air and maritime domains.
This shift represents an opportunity to expand the scope of contracts from selling platforms to providing software updates, mission packages, operational and maintenance services, and ongoing support.
U.S. Navy Continues Investing in Uncrewed Maritime Systems
Developments in the GARC contract illustrate the scale of commercial opportunity that may arise following initial platform deliveries; BlackSea completed the delivery of 325 uncrewed vessels to the U.S. Navy during 2025, in the first large-scale procurement of this class of vessels in U.S. Navy history.
However, investment did not stop at vessel delivery; the total contract value rose to approximately $350 million during 2026, following the addition of funding of nearly $135 million to upgrade systems and expand their operational capabilities.
Upgrades include transitioning to the Lynx architecture, adding autonomy and command and control capabilities, and integrating new mission packages, alongside continued vessel operation and support.
The company also secured a $41.6 million contract to provide GARC platforms and new marine systems with mine countermeasures packages, enabling the execution of integrated missions from mine detection to neutralization.
This reveals an economic model that goes beyond equipment sales, relying on upgrading existing platforms and turning them into multi-mission systems, creating additional revenue opportunities after initial delivery.
$16.6 Billion Pipeline… Future Opportunities, Not Confirmed Revenue
AEVEX’s volume of future commercial opportunities rose to approximately $16.6 billion, compared to $10.5 billion in the previous quarter, an increase of nearly 58%.
These opportunities include long-range drone projects, one-way attack systems, maritime systems, and support missions for several U.S. military commands.
However, this figure represents potential multi-year commercial opportunities, encompassing funded and unfunded programs, and does not represent confirmed contracts or guaranteed revenue.
In contrast, the funded backlog of contracts reached approximately $444.3 million at the end of the quarter, while the company holds about $1.1 billion in awarded contracts that have not yet received full funding.
Management expects to convert about $410 million of these unfunded contracts into revenue by the end of 2027, providing greater growth visibility without factoring in any new competitive contracts.

candidates.snippet: Mercor $750M Series D at $20B: What It Means CASRAI
candidates.text:
On 10 November 2026, Mercor announced a $750 million Series D round at a $20 billion valuation. The company runs a marketplace that pays domain experts to train and evaluate frontier AI models, and the round doubles the $10 billion valuation it set in October 2025.
What was announced
Mercor published the news on its own blog on 10 November 2026. The round was priced at $20 billion and included an employee tender alongside new investment. Named participants were Benchmark, Felicis, Fundomo, funds managed by affiliates of Apollo, G Squared, General Catalyst, Glade Brook Capital, NVIDIA, Salesforce, Sapphire Ventures, StepStone Group, XTX Ventures and Zoom. The announcement did not name a lead investor. Crunchbase News listed the round among the week’s biggest funding rounds in its 13 November 2026 roundup.
The previous round was a $350 million Series C at a $10 billion valuation in October 2025, reported by TechCrunch . TechCrunch also reported in July 2026 that Mercor was in talks at a $20 billion valuation .
What Mercor says it does
In the announcement, Mercor says it has more than five million experts in its network “getting paid to train frontier AI models based on their unique knowledge”. It also says it works with enterprises and experts in their fields to build custom evaluations based on the company’s actual workflows. The company says the new funding will go toward infrastructure and research for evaluations and post-training, and toward environments where AI agents can learn complex workflows. It also says it has opened offices in New York and London. The announcement does not break down the network by qualification, so it does not say how many of those experts hold doctorates or work as researchers.
Why it matters for researchers and research offices
The round is a data point on how much capital is flowing toward expert human judgment as an input to AI development. Three practical questions follow for universities and research offices. These are editorial observations, not claims made by Mercor.
Researcher time. Expert annotation and evaluation work for AI companies is paid outside the normal grant and appointment structures. Research offices may need to check how it interacts with institutional outside-activity and conflict-of-commitment policies.
Confidential and unpublished material. Evaluation tasks built from real workflows raise questions about what a researcher may share, including unpublished data, grant content or material under a confidentiality agreement.
Evaluation methods. Expert-written tests are one way AI developers measure model ability. Researchers who read results from such tests can use frameworks such as model evaluation suites and AI evaluation cards to ask what was tested and how.
For background on the techniques this market supports, see RLHF and training data provenance . For an example of a research-level expert-written benchmark, see FrontierMath .
What is not yet known
The Series D announcement did not disclose revenue, expert pay rates or the share of the network made up of researchers. Anyone weighing the opportunity should rely on the terms they are offered directly rather than on funding headlines.

Agile Robots Hits $8.5bn Valuation as SoftBank and NVIDIA Back $500m Funding Round
The Munich-based robotics company Agile Robots has secured $500 million in fresh funding, putting it among Europe’s most highly valued private robotics businesses as investors look beyond generative AI towards industrial automation.
Munich, 15 November 2026 – Agile Robots , the German Physical AI company, has raised $500 million in a Series F funding round at a valuation of $8.5 billion , according to an announcement issued on 12 November.
Led by SoftBank Group, the round attracted investment from NVIDIA, Hitachi Group – including Hitachi and Hitachi Ventures – and T.Capital, among others. It brings the Munich-based company’s total funding raised to $2 billion.
The investment comes as the artificial intelligence industry increasingly turns its attention to machines capable of performing physical tasks. For Agile Robots, the challenge is no longer simply developing intelligent robotics technology, but producing and deploying it economically at industrial scale.
Agile Robots Funding: Key Facts
Company: Agile Robots
Headquarters: Munich, Germany
Founded: 2018
Funding round: Series F
Capital raised: $500 million
Company valuation: $8.5 billion
Total funding raised: $2 billion
Lead investor: SoftBank Group
Other investors: NVIDIA, Hitachi Group and T.Capital
Industry: Physical AI, robotics and industrial automation
Global deployments: More than 20,000 industrial robotic solutions, according to the company
Expansion plans: United States, Germany and additional international markets
Funding announcement: 12 November 2026
From Artificial Intelligence to Physical AI
Founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), Agile Robots develops robotic systems that combine artificial intelligence, sensors and precision engineering.
Its products range from industrial robotic arms and dexterous hands to mobile and humanoid robots, supported by proprietary software and AI models.
The distinction between conventional automation and Physical AI is commercially significant. Traditional industrial robots generally perform predefined tasks in structured environments. AI-enabled systems aim to interpret changing conditions and adapt their behaviour accordingly.
That could open up more complex activities in manufacturing, logistics and electronics assembly, where tasks have historically depended on human dexterity and judgement.
Yet technical capability alone will not determine adoption. Manufacturers must be convinced that these systems can operate safely, reliably and at a cost that justifies replacing or supplementing existing processes.
SoftBank and NVIDIA Back Industrial-Scale Robotics
SoftBank’s decision to lead the latest funding round, alongside NVIDIA’s participation, puts Agile Robots in the spotlight as investors seek commercial applications for artificial intelligence beyond software.
The new capital will finance international expansion, further robotics development and additional manufacturing capacity.
Dr Zhaopeng Chen, founder and chief executive of Agile Robots, sees Physical AI as a fundamental shift in how industrial work is organised.
“Physical AI will fundamentally change how the world builds, moves and makes things. Our vision is intelligent robots working alongside people in factories and warehouses everywhere, and Agile Robots is determined to lead that shift,” Chen said.
Dennis Chang, Managing Partner at SoftBank Investment Advisers, highlighted the importance of translating research into commercial deployment.
“We believe Physical AI will transform industries. Agile Robots combines deep robotics expertise with the ability to execute at industrial scale, enabling it to bring Physical AI into everyday operations,” Chang said.
The participation of prominent technology investors gives Agile Robots additional financial backing, although the announcement does not disclose individual investment amounts or the terms of the funding round.

Viasat: $450 Million U.S. Space Force Contract For Golden Dome Space Data Network Backbone Development
Viasat, a Carlsbad, California-based provider of satellite communications and secure networking technologies, has received an indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract with a ceiling of $450 million from the U.S. Space Force’s Space Systems Command (SSC). The award will support the development, deployment, sustainment, and operation of the Space Data Network Backbone (SDN-B) mission operations center, a critical component of the military’s efforts to establish resilient space-based communications infrastructure supporting Golden Dome for America and Joint Force operations.
The contract includes an initial $115 million task order to support development and scaling of the mission operations center and associated network operations capabilities.
The $450 million represents the maximum value available under the IDIQ contract rather than a guaranteed payment to Viasat. Additional work will depend on future task orders and government requirements.
The award positions Viasat as a network and mission systems integration partner supporting the Space Force’s efforts to establish a more interconnected and resilient military space architecture.
The SDN-B initiative is designed to provide high-capacity, low-latency data transport across multiple satellite networks and orbital environments.
Its architecture will support communications requirements for the U.S. Space Force, Golden Dome for America, and military operations conducted by the Joint Force worldwide.
Supporting The Golden Dome Space Data Network Backbone
The Space Data Network Backbone is a multi-vendor data transport architecture designed to connect and manage communications capabilities across participating space and ground systems.
The network is intended to provide resilient connectivity for military operations that depend on timely access to information collected and transmitted through space-based infrastructure.
Rather than relying on a single satellite operator or communications architecture, SDN-B is designed to integrate multiple providers and network elements.
This approach supports the Space Force’s broader objective of developing open architectures that can incorporate commercial technologies and adapt to changing mission requirements.
Viasat will focus on the mission operations center responsible for supporting network management and integration under government direction.
The center is intended to provide a coordinated view of participating SDN-B network elements, allowing operators to monitor connectivity, network performance, and operational status.
The infrastructure will also support government-directed prioritization of communications resources based on military mission requirements.

The initial $115 million task order will fund work associated with establishing and scaling the SDN-B mission operations center and its network operations capabilities.
Viasat will apply its experience operating secure satellite communications networks to support the development of an enterprise-level operational infrastructure.
The company’s responsibilities include systems engineering, network integration, operational support, and sustainment activities.
The mission operations center will provide tools to manage participating connectivity services and support a common operational picture of the network.
These capabilities are intended to help military operators understand the status and performance of the communications infrastructure supporting their missions.
The contract also provides a framework for future engineering, operational, and sustainment work as the SDN-B architecture develops.
Additional task orders may support evolving requirements involving network availability, cybersecurity, and resilience.

The objective is to create an integrated operational environment capable of coordinating communications resources across multiple providers.

LangChain Raises $300 Million Series C at $3 Billion Valuation to Advance Enterprise AI Agents
By Ash Kate November 14, 2026
Article content
LangChain Secures $300 Million to Advance Enterprise AI Agents
LangChain has raised $300 million in a Series C funding round at a $3 billion valuation, strengthening its position in the rapidly expanding enterprise AI agent market. The round was led by existing investor CapitalG , with significant participation from new investors GIC and DFJ Growth, alongside existing investors IVP and Sapphire Ventures.
The latest funding brings LangChain's total capital raised to approximately $460 million. The investment comes as businesses increasingly explore AI agents to automate workflows, develop intelligent applications and transform internal operations.
The company plans to use the funding to advance its mission of enabling every organisation to own its intelligence, with a focus on giving businesses greater control over the models, data and infrastructure powering their AI systems.
Expanding LangSmith's Enterprise AI Capabilities
At the centre of LangChain's strategy is LangSmith, its framework-agnostic platform designed to help organisations run, improve and govern AI agents.
The company reports that more than 7,000 organisations already rely on LangSmith, spanning fast-growing technology companies and large enterprises. Its customers include Harvey, Rippling and Listen Labs, alongside NVIDIA, Toyota and Salesforce.
LangChain is developing its platform around three core capabilities: Agent Runtime, Agent Improvement and Agent Governance.
Agent Runtime provides the infrastructure and tools required to build, deploy and operate agents reliably. Agent Improvement focuses on observability, evaluation and continuous performance optimisation, while Agent Governance gives organisations greater control over model usage, data protection, tool access and authentication.
These capabilities address some of the operational challenges businesses encounter when moving AI agents from experimentation into production environments.
Building Greater Control Over Enterprise Intelligence
LangChain's funding announcement reflects a broader shift in enterprise AI adoption, where the focus is moving beyond building AI-powered applications towards managing intelligent systems at scale.
The company believes domain-specific agents, differentiated by their knowledge, data and user experience, will play an increasingly important role in both standalone software products and internal business operations.
Its approach centres on giving organisations the flexibility to choose models, maintain control over their data and infrastructure, and continuously improve their agents without being restricted to a single model ecosystem.
LangChain also highlighted customer deployments that demonstrate the platform's enterprise applications. According to the company, Clay uses LangSmith to monitor hundreds of millions of agent runs each month, while Workday has reduced the time required to deploy a new agent from five months to under a day.
The company is also preparing to introduce additional LangSmith capabilities at a dedicated release event scheduled for November 20, 2026.
Investor Confidence in the Agentic AI Infrastructure Market
The Series C brings together a combination of existing backers and new institutional investors. Beyond the lead investors, LangChain also welcomed Salesforce Ventures, Insight Venture Partners, QuantumLight and MongoDB Ventures, while Sequoia, Amplify and Benchmark increased their investments.
The $3 billion valuation represents a significant increase from the $1.25 billion valuation associated with the company's previous $125 million funding round in October 2025.
The latest investment signals continued investor interest in the infrastructure supporting enterprise AI adoption, particularly platforms focused on making AI agents more reliable, observable and manageable in production environments.
About LangChain
LangChain develops open-source frameworks and enterprise tools that help organisations build and manage AI agents. Its product ecosystem includes LangChain, LangGraph and Deep Agents, alongside LangSmith, a platform for testing, deploying, monitoring and governing AI agents across their development lifecycle.

candidates.text:
Skilled welders are hard to find, and shipyards and heavy-equipment plants are sitting on full order books. Traditional industrial robots do not help much here. They follow pre-programmed paths, which makes them a poor fit for welds that differ slightly from one part to the next. Path Robotics , a Columbus, Ohio-based startup, is betting that a robot that can see and decide for itself can fill that gap. On Nov. 10, the company announced a $300 million Series E at a $2.45 billion post-money valuation.
Georgian , an AI-focused growth equity firm, led the round. NAVER Ventures and D. E. Shaw Ventures joined as new investors, and existing backers Addition, Drive Capital, IronArc Ventures, Tiger Global, and Yamaha Motor Ventures also took part. Georgian partner Emily Walsh will join Path’s board.
Giving the robot eyes and judgment
A conventional welding robot has to be taught its path step by step, and a part that sits slightly out of place can ruin the weld. Path’s physical AI welding model, Obsidian, takes that teaching out of the loop. The robot finds the weld joint on its own, plans the sequence and path, welds, and adjusts when conditions change mid-job. The model learns from real-world welding data. For a factory, that means variable welds without reprogramming the robot each time.
The company recently added Rove, a mobile welding system that puts Obsidian on a quadruped robot. Instead of bringing the part to a welding cell, the robot walks to the part. Path says it shows the same model can run on different robot bodies.
ARR up 17x in 18 months, led by shipbuilding and defense
Path says its annual recurring revenue grew 17-fold over the past 18 months, though it did not disclose a dollar figure. The growth has come from shipbuilding and defense, heavy equipment, and energy infrastructure. Customers include HII, the largest U.S. shipbuilder, Lockheed Martin, and the maritime defense company Saronic , along with mid-sized manufacturers such as EK Machine, Millerbernd Manufacturing, TransAmerican Power Products, and TYCROP. Earlier this year, Path announced a $600 million performance-based production agreement with HII to deploy physical AI across U.S. Navy shipbuilding programs. Headcount has grown 97% over the past year, and the company plans to reach 400 employees by year-end.
CEO and co-founder Andy Lonsberry said Path started with welding because it is one of the hardest jobs on the factory floor to automate. “Our goal isn’t to automate one step, but to automate the entire factory,” he said. Founded in 2018, Path has now raised more than $610 million. The new money will go toward scaling the welding business, expanding to tasks before and after welding and to new robot form factors, and training AI models.
Georgian pointed to Path’s proprietary models and its growing base of production data, which it said improves the system with every deployment. Lockheed Martin Ventures called the investment an important milestone for strengthening the U.S. defense industrial base.
Competition: welding specialists and general-purpose robot AI
A handful of newer companies are going after the same problem. Korea’s RB-Ware makes a no-code welding robot and has installed more than 250 units in 16 countries, and NeoArcRobotics is building cutting and welding robots for Korean shipyards. Augmentus raised $11 million to scale physical AI for robotic welding, and China’s LE Robotics raised tens of millions of yuan in a Series A+ round in February. None has raised anything close to Path’s total.
Others are chasing general-purpose robot intelligence rather than one task. Skild AI and Physical Intelligence are building foundation models meant to run on any robot, and defense manufacturer Hadrian raised $1.37 billion in a Series D in August to rebuild U.S. manufacturing capacity. Where those companies bet on a universal model or on the factory itself, Path is trying to perfect the hardest single process first and then extend to the steps around it.

candidates.text:
Money is pouring into companies that build quantum computers. Oratomic raised a $475 million Series B in October, and Universal Quantum closed a Series A of more than $100 million. But whether qubits are made from neutral atoms or trapped ions, the problem is the same: they are sensitive to noise and make errors mid-calculation. Q-CTRL , an Australian company that sells software to reduce those errors, said it raised a $290 million Series C (A$415 million). It says the round makes it the newest quantum unicorn, though it did not disclose a valuation.
Software that makes other companies’ chips usable
Q-CTRL does not build quantum computers. Founded in 2017 by Michael Biercuk , a University of Sydney physicist, it sells software that helps machines built by other companies run better. It pitches a hardware-agnostic design that is not tied to any one qubit technology.
It has two main products. Fire Opal is cloud software that automatically shortens the quantum circuits a developer writes, maps them onto a chip according to each machine’s error profile and corrects measurement errors before returning results. It runs on IBM’s quantum service, IonQ and Rigetti systems and Amazon Braket, among others, and the company claims it can run circuits up to 10 times deeper on the same hardware. Boulder Opal is for those who build or operate quantum computers. Even after it is switched on, a quantum computer needs its control signals tuned qubit by qubit, and the product automates that calibration and upkeep without a team of physicists. It supports superconducting and semiconductor spin-qubit machines, with trapped-ion and neutral-atom support available on request, the company says. Its target customers are chipmakers and data center and HPC operators. In computing, the company also claims a 3,000x speedup in materials discovery for the energy sector.
The third business pairs software with sensors. Ironstone Opal is a navigation system for places where GPS is unavailable or jammed. It measures tiny variations in the Earth’s magnetic field and matches them against a magnetic map to find its position. The company builds the quantum magnetometers itself, and AI software filters out the magnetic interference the aircraft generates. The company says the system is 100 times better than the best alternative, but in its published flight trial it reported up to 50 times lower positioning uncertainty than an inertial navigation system. It says Ironstone Opal is being deployed on commercial aircraft with Airbus, on autonomous platforms with Lockheed Martin and on drones. All performance figures come from the company.
Led by Salesforce Ventures, expanded twice
Salesforce Ventures led the round, with Bullhound Capital and Affinity Partners named as headline participants. The company says it expanded the round twice to meet investor demand and calls it the largest raise by a software-focused quantum company. Q-CTRL expanded its Series B to $113 million in October 2024.
New investors are Affinity Partners, AMD Ventures, EDGE Group, MPower Partners, Australia’s National Reconstruction Fund Corporation and SPARX Asset Management. Returning investors are Alpha Edison, Alumni Ventures, Bullhound Capital, DCVC, In-Q-Tel, Lockheed Martin Ventures, Main Sequence, Ridgeline, Salesforce Ventures, Salus Ventures and Square Peg. The company says the mix of strategic, private equity and growth-stage venture investors positions it to scale through joint sales, technology integration and direct revenue.
Salesforce Ventures said the hard problem in quantum is getting useful output from the machine, not building it. It pointed to a materials simulation run on IBM hardware that developers can call directly from the IBM Quantum Platform, and to what it described as the first quantum navigation system qualified for safety of flight. Bullhound called Q-CTRL one of the few quantum companies with real customers and real revenue, and MPower Partners said it wants to help expand the company’s footprint in Japan.
Q-CTRL plans to use the funds to double down on software, scale globally across sectors such as finance and energy, and continue its autonomy and aerospace programs. Biercuk said the company’s core value is delivering real customer value from quantum technology, which is why it focuses on infrastructure software. The company did not disclose revenue, total funding to date or customer counts.
Competitors: the same software layer, and hardware makers building their own
Q-CTRL’s pitch is that errors remain no matter which qubit technology wins. The quantum computer makers Wowtale has covered span neutral atoms (Oratomic and Atom Computing ), trapped ions (Universal Quantum), superconducting qubits ( Qilimanjaro ) and photonics ( PsiQuantum ), and no winner has emerged. Such hardware makers are a potential customer base for software like Q-CTRL’s, though none is confirmed as a Q-CTRL partner.
In the same software layer, QEDMA tackles the problem closest to Fire Opal’s. The Israeli company’s QESEM software analyzes each device’s noise pattern, suppresses some errors and mitigates the rest in post-processing, and it is offered through IBM’s Qiskit Functions catalog. QEDMA raised a $26 million Series A in July 2025 with participation from IBM and Korea Investment Partners. Quantum Machines makes control hardware for quantum computers and raised a $170 million Series C ; its CEO has said more than half of the companies in the field use its technology. Because Boulder Opal supports its controllers, it is both a rival and a complement. Britain’s Riverlane builds error-correction chips and software and raised a $75 million Series C in August 2024. Classiq makes quantum circuit design software, raised a $110 million Series C in May 2025 and is integrated with Fire Opal.

Courtesy Photo
November 15th, 2026 | Nebraska Attorney General’s Office
Lincoln – Attorney General Mike Hilgers announced a $183.5 million multistate settlement with Acima Digital, LLC, and its parent company, Acima Holdings, LLC. The settlement includes $43 million in consumer restitution, $10.5 million to participating states, and $130 million in lease balance reductions. Nebraska will receive more than $292,608.42 in restitution and $593,465.05 in lease forgiveness for Nebraska consumers.
Acima, a rent-to-own financing company that partners with Nebraska retailers, was accused of misleading consumers about the terms and costs of its rental-purchase agreements. Forty-three states alleged that Acima advertised 90-day payoff programs without clearly disclosing that consumers were automatically placed in 12-month agreements and could end up paying twice the advertised cash price. The company also allegedly misrepresented its services as traditional credit, marked up merchandise prices, and made it difficult for consumers to return merchandise and end agreements.
Under the settlement, Acima must improve retail partner training, provide clearer advertising and contract disclosures, stop marking up merchandise prices, allow consumers to return merchandise without obstruction, and properly address delivery, damage, and repair issues. The company also cannot report rental-purchase agreements to the three major credit bureaus for five years.
Consumers eligible for restitution or lease forgiveness do not need to take action. The settlement administrator will contact consumers receiving restitution, while Acima will notify those eligible for lease forgiveness.

ATTORNEY GENERAL TONG ANNOUNCES $183.5 MILLION MULTISTATE SETTLEMENT WITH RENT-TO-OWN COMPANY ACIMA DIGITAL
(Hartford, CT) — Attorney General William Tong today announced a $183.5 million multistate settlement with Acima Digital, LLC and its parent company, Acima Holdings, LLC, resolving allegations that the rent-to-own finance company misled consumers about its agreements and deceptively marked up prices.
The settlement consists of $43 million in consumer restitution, $130 million in lease balance reductions, and a $10.5 million payment to the states. Connecticut consumers will receive $2,441,257 in lease forgiveness, in addition to the $246,090.70 payment to the state.
Consumers who are eligible to obtain restitution or lease forgiveness pursuant to this settlement do not need to take any action. Consumers eligible to receive restitution will be contacted by the settlement administrator, Rust Consulting. Consumers who are eligible to receive lease forgiveness will be contacted by Acima.
Acima partners with retailers to offer financing to consumers via rental-purchase agreements. The settlement resolves allegations that Acima deceptively advertised its rental-purchase agreements in manner that misled consumers about the nature and cost of its rental-purchase agreements and deceptively marked up the cash price of the merchandise being rented, amongst other deceptive acts and practices with respect to the consummation and servicing of its rental-purchase agreements and its debt collection and credit reporting practices.
“Acima lured and locked consumers into overpriced rent-to-own deals by obscuring key information, including the length of these agreements, the total cost, and options for termination. They took advantage of families struggling to afford basic needs, and we are making them pay. Our settlement sends millions of dollars back to consumers and forces strict reforms to ensure fair and honest practices going forward,” said Attorney General Tong.
The multistate coalition of 43 states alleged that Acima marketed its rental-purchase agreements as 90-day pay off programs without disclosing that consumers were automatically defaulted into the maximum 12-month term whereby consumers could pay approximately two times the cash price advertised by Acima’s retail partner. Acima also advertised its rental-purchase product using terms like “credit,” which often misled consumers into believing that they were obtaining traditional financing. Acima’s process for electronically executing rental-purchase agreements also obscured the terms of the transaction, further compounding consumer confusion. Additionally, Acima obstructed consumers’ ability to terminate their rental-purchase agreements without penalty by returning their merchandise to Acima.
Under the settlement, Acima has agreed to injunctive terms to address these practices, including to:
• Conduct robust training of its retail partners;
• Refrain from making certain representations in its advertising unless other material information is clearly and conspicuously disclosed;
• Refrain from obscuring the material terms and conditions of its rental-purchase agreements during Acima’s electronic signature process;
• Refrain from marking up the cash price from that of Acima’s retail partners;
• Refrain from obstructing consumers’ ability to terminate their rental-purchase agreements by returning the merchandise to Acima;
• Refrain from reporting rental-purchase agreements to the big three credit reporting agencies for a period of five years; and
• Properly handle late deliveries, merchandise damaged at the time of delivery, and adhere to legal obligations to make repairs to merchandise during the course of the lease.
The state attorneys general that joined Attorney General Tong in today’s settlement are Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, Minnesota, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Nevada, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia, Wisconsin, and Wyoming.
Assistant Attorneys General Joseph Gasser and Addison Keilty and Deputy Associate Attorney General Michael Wertheimer, Chief of the Consumer Protection Section assisted the Attorney General in this matter.

Windward Bio has raised $175 million in its US initial public offering, adding to a growing pipeline of healthcare and biotechnology companies tapping public markets as listings in other sectors face pressure from economic uncertainty.
The Basel, Switzerland-based drug developer sold approximately 10.3 million shares at $17 each, within its marketed range of $16 to $18. Its shares are scheduled to begin trading on Friday on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol WWB.
The offering gives Windward fresh capital to advance its experimental antibody medicines for serious respiratory and dermatological diseases, with its lead programme targeting conditions that affect millions of patients worldwide. The company is backed by Novo Holdings, alongside other healthcare investors, and has attracted a $50 million commitment from French pharmaceutical group Sanofi.

Sanofi agreed to purchase $50 million in shares and pre-funded warrants through a private placement, providing Windward with an additional source of institutional backing as it enters the public market. The investment also gives the pharmaceutical group exposure to a biotechnology company developing treatments in areas where demand for new therapies remains significant.
Windward’s lead candidate, WIN378, is being developed for asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or COPD. The antibody is designed to block a protein involved in airway inflammation, an approach intended to address an underlying biological mechanism contributing to both conditions.
The programme will be central to the company’s development strategy as it moves into the public market. However, WIN378 remains an experimental medicine, and its commercial prospects will depend on clinical results, regulatory approvals and its ability to demonstrate meaningful benefits over existing treatments.
Led by founder and chief executive Luca Santarelli, Windward has raised $310 million in equity financing from Novo Holdings and other healthcare investors, including OrbiMed, Blue Owl and RTW Investments.
Santarelli has previously built biotechnology businesses that attracted substantial acquisition interest from larger pharmaceutical companies. VectivBio, one of his earlier ventures, was acquired by Ironwood Pharmaceuticals for $1.2 billion in 2023. Pfizer acquired another company he was associated with, Therachon, in 2019 for $810 million.
That history provides Windward with a management team familiar with biotechnology development and the commercial pressures facing companies seeking to bring new medicines to market. However, previous acquisitions do not guarantee that its current drug candidates will achieve similar outcomes.
The company’s IPO also underscores the importance of specialist healthcare investors in financing drug development. Biotechnology companies often require substantial capital over several years before generating commercial revenue, as clinical trials, regulatory submissions, and manufacturing preparations result in costs well ahead of product launches.
Public listings can provide access to a broader pool of capital, but they also expose early-stage drug developers to market volatility and greater scrutiny of clinical progress. For Windward, the challenge will be to use its new funding to advance its pipeline while showing that its scientific approach can translate into viable treatments.
Windward’s listing comes during a period of renewed activity among healthcare and biotechnology companies seeking to enter US public markets. The sector has accounted for a series of listings this autumn, even as macroeconomic headwinds have weakened IPO activity in other industries.
The contrast indicates that investor appetite for new listings remains selective rather than broadly restored. Companies with specialized healthcare programmes and established institutional backing have found opportunities to raise capital, while uncertainty over economic conditions and market valuations continues to weigh on other potential issuers.
For biotechnology businesses, the appeal of public markets is closely tied to the need for long-term financing. Unlike companies with established cash-generating operations, drug developers must often fund research and clinical trials before they can establish whether a candidate has commercial potential. A successful IPO can extend their financial runway and support development milestones that may improve their prospects of securing partnerships or attracting acquisition interest.
Still, investors face considerable risks. Drug candidates can fail in clinical trials, regulatory authorities can request additional evidence, and even approved treatments may struggle to gain market share. These make Windward’s valuation depend not only on its scientific programmes but also on the pace and quality of clinical data it produces.
Jefferies, TD Cowen, Piper Sandler and UBS Investment Bank are underwriting the offering.
Another Swiss healthcare-related company, dental firm vVardis, is also expected to go public on Friday. Its planned listing alongside Windward would add to the week’s activity and provide another indication of investor demand for companies operating in specialized healthcare markets.

Before Trump Eased Nvidia Chip Exports to China, He Bought $160 Million in Stock, Raising Conflict-of-Interest Questions
Add preferred source
1
U.S. President Donald Trump has been revealed to have purchased $1 million to $5 million worth of Nvidia stock (approximately NT$33 million to NT$160 million) just before rescinding the Biden administration's AI chip export controls, and to have made at least three additional purchases of $250,000 to $500,000 each after opening H200 chip sales to China. An anti-corruption organization is questioning the intersection of policy shifts and personal financial interests. The controversy deepened after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid suspicions of involvement with an alleged Chinese spy. Democrats have launched an investigation, leaving Nvidia's China business prospects facing dual policy and political uncertainties.
Key Elements
Donald Trump Nvidia Jensen Huang Alice Huang DeKleptocracy U.S. Department of Commerce H200 chips AI Diffusion Framework Megaspeed The Guardian Council on Foreign Relations
U.S. President Donald Trump has been revealed to have made large purchases of Nvidia stock on the eve of rescinding the previous administration's AI chip export controls, triggering strong questions about the intersection of policy and personal financial interests. According to an analysis by anti-corruption organization DeKleptocracy of Trump's public financial disclosure filings, Trump purchased $1 million to $5 million worth of Nvidia shares (approximately NT$33 million to NT$160 million) just days before scrapping the Biden administration's "Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion" in May of last year.
The policy had originally established tiered management of AI chip exports based on each country's diplomatic and security relationship with the United States, with allies such as South Korea placed in a relatively permissive category, while China, Russia, and North Korea faced the strictest export blockades. The core purpose of the Biden administration's framework was to slow China's acquisition of advanced computing power and thereby its ability to build up its own AI capabilities. The Trump administration decided to scrap the entire framework on the grounds that it hindered American corporate innovation, imposed unnecessary regulatory burdens, and effectively relegated dozens of countries to "second-tier" status in a way that could damage diplomatic relations.
The timing overlap makes this transaction particularly sensitive. Had the framework actually taken effect, Nvidia's shipments to China—a market that once contributed about a quarter of its sales—would have been significantly constrained. After Trump announced the rescission of the controls, Nvidia's stock price promptly rose. The disclosure filings also show that Trump simultaneously purchased shares in tech giants including Apple, Meta, and Microsoft, rather than betting solely on Nvidia.
The controversy does not end there. In December 2025, Trump further announced that Nvidia would be allowed to sell H200 chips to approved customers in China, and the U.S. Department of Commerce formally granted approval in January 2026. The H200 was one of Nvidia's most advanced products at the time, with experts estimating its performance at roughly six times that of the chips China could obtain at the time. Disclosure filings show that after the export-opening announcement, Trump made at least three more Nvidia stock purchases, each in the range of $250,001 to $500,000 (approximately NT$16 million). Counting all records since taking office, the related trades have reached dozens.
DeKleptocracy stated bluntly that while the United States is still debating whether a suspected Chinese spy manipulated White House policy to profit an AI company, it must equally confront whether Trump's financial interests prompted him to hand the AI industry's critical technology to China.
At the center of the storm is Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. According to The Guardian, Huang had an extramarital affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, who is alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence. This relationship enabled Megaspeed, Alice Huang's Singapore-based cloud computing company, to obtain billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia chips at a time when other operators could scarcely secure supply. Jensen Huang has announced his resignation following the exposure of the affair.
Jensen Huang has long been regarded as a close ally of Trump, and the two have met multiple times. Nvidia also donated $25 million (approximately NT$820 million) in October 2025 to support the construction of the Trump White House ballroom project, with Huang stating at the time that he was pleased to participate.
The Council on Foreign Relations has warned that allowing the H200 could substantially boost the computing capacity of China's AI factories, effectively adding fuel to the fire for America's primary competitor.
Political pursuit has already begun. It is understood that U.S. Democrats have initiated proceedings to investigate the political-business relationship between Trump and Jensen Huang, as well as the decision-making process behind the easing of semiconductor export controls.
The significance of this episode for the market goes beyond a single stock-disclosure controversy. Nvidia's China business prospects are now tied simultaneously to national security reviews and the White House occupant's personal financial records. Any advancement of congressional investigations or convening of hearings could reignite market concerns about the flip-flopping of export policy. For investors, whether H200 exports to China can proceed smoothly and whether the channel through which Megaspeed obtained chips will be pursued are two key indicators for gauging the visibility of Nvidia's China revenue.

MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
