MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
MaxCyte has agreed to acquire Akron BioProducts from affiliates of Arcline Investment Management for $151.8 million. The transaction is expected to close before the end of 2026, subject to customary conditions.
Akron Bio supplies Good Manufacturing Practice-grade reagents and ancillary materials used across cell therapy manufacturing. Its products include cytokines, growth factors, human plasma-derived materials, specialty media, and other consumables.
The acquisition will expand MaxCyte beyond its historical focus on nonviral cell engineering. Akron’s products are used in both viral and nonviral workflows at stages ranging from cell expansion through cryopreservation.
The combined company’s technologies are incorporated into five commercially approved therapies and support more than 100 clinical programs. Both businesses maintain drug master files referenced in customers’ regulatory submissions, creating long-term connections to validated manufacturing processes.
Akron is expected to produce approximately $28 million in 2026 revenue and between $7 million and $8 million of EBITDA. MaxCyte expects the acquisition to nearly double its revenue base, increase recurring consumables revenue, and accelerate its path toward profitability.
The companies have limited customer overlap despite serving similar biopharmaceutical markets. MaxCyte therefore expects to use its commercial infrastructure to introduce Akron products to additional customers and pursue cross-selling opportunities.
The buyer projects that Akron’s positive cash flow will help reduce the combined company’s annual cash burn to less than $10 million in 2027. MaxCyte expects to hold approximately $40 million to $45 million of cash when the transaction closes.
The consideration consists of $105 million in cash, subject to adjustments, 20,639,733 MaxCyte shares valued at approximately $26.8 million, and $20 million of guaranteed deferred payments. The deferred amount will be paid in two $10 million installments in January 2028 and January 2029.
MaxCyte has also secured a credit facility of up to $75 million from MidCap Financial, consisting of a $55 million term loan and a $20 million revolver. It plans to draw $20 million from the term loan and $2 million from the revolver at closing.
Akron will continue operating under its existing brand, with its management team and employees remaining part of the combined organization.
KEY QUOTES
“The acquisition of Akron marks an exciting new chapter for MaxCyte. This acquisition represents a significant step forward for us, expanding our presence across the viral and non-viral cell therapy development and manufacturing workflow, while projecting to nearly double our revenue base and accelerate our path to profitability. From day one, Akron provides us with an established portfolio of clinical and commercial programs supported by Akron’s DMFs and reagents. By bringing together two highly complementary businesses, we are diversifying our revenue base, increasing our mix of recurring revenue and expanding our exposure to the growth of commercially approved cell therapies, positioning MaxCyte for more durable near- and long-term growth. Like MaxCyte, Akron has become a trusted supplier to leading biopharma companies by delivering differentiated, high-quality products and best-in-class service. Akron is a market leader in the mission-critical consumables required for cell therapy manufacturing, including cytokines, growth factors, human plasma-derived products and media. We are excited to work alongside the talented Akron team as we bring together two companies to deepen customer relationships and better support cell therapy developers from development through commercialization.”
Maher Masoud, President and CEO of MaxCyte
“We are tremendously excited by the opportunity to join these two world-class organizations, leveraging our collective experience and expertise to support our partners as they bring transformative therapies to patients around the world. At Akron, we have always believed in earning our partners’ trust through consistent execution, uncompromising quality, and a deep commitment to the patients they serve. As part of MaxCyte, we remain committed to delivering the quality, reliability, and innovation our partners have come to expect.”
Ezequiel Zylberberg, COO of Akron Bio
“Akron Bio’s success reflects the dedication of its team, and we believe MaxCyte is the best partner to drive continued growth and expand its impact on patients. Our decision to accept MaxCyte shares as part of the consideration reflects our confidence in the combined company’s long-term value and allows us to participate in its future success.”

candidates.snippet: Vumedi Raises $140M Series B, Oakland Health Tech Hoodline
candidates.text:
555 12th St. — Oakland Street Scene
Google Street View
An Oakland health-tech company has raised $140 million in a new funding round. Vumedi, which builds an AI-powered learning platform for physicians, has raised $140 million in Series B funding, with plans to pour the money into talent, research and development, product development and outreach as it expands its clinical learning tools.
The investment came from Oak HC/FT, according to FinSMEs , which reported the round. Vumedi is led by founder and CEO Roman Giverts, and the company describes its platform as a tool that connects clinicians with specialists and peers so they can learn procedures, evaluate treatments and navigate complex cases, the outlet reports.
What the Platform Actually Does
At the center of Vumedi's pitch is scale paired with AI. The platform uses artificial intelligence to turn more than 100,000 physician-led videos and nearly 5,000 podcast episodes, spanning more than 21 medical specialties, into what the company calls an on-demand clinical resource, per the same report. Rather than leaving clinicians to sift through hours of footage, the system synthesizes multiple expert perspectives and links directly to time-stamped segments within videos.
The company says its platform now serves more than 150,000 NPI-verified clinicians and generated over 56 million minutes of learning over the past 12 months. Back in a 2018 interview, Giverts described Vumedi's mission as helping physicians make the best care decisions through what he called unbiased video education in an interview with MPO-mag.com . That same article reported the platform then had roughly 250,000 physician users and 20,000 videos contributed by more than 5,000 healthcare organizations and professionals, including partnerships with 150 hospitals and conferences such as Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic and Johns Hopkins.
Funding Figures Don't All Line Up
Not every account of Vumedi's fundraising history tells the same story. A snippet from 01net referenced a $104 million investment from Oak HC/FT, though it's unclear from that report whether it describes the same financing as the newly reported $140 million round or a separate transaction. Separately, CB Insights lists Vumedi's most recent funding round as a $79.98 million Series B dated May 22, 2025, and puts the company's total raised at $82.08 million across four rounds. The available reporting does not reconcile these differing figures with the $140 million sum reported this week.
Part of a Broader AI Health-Tech Wave
Vumedi's raise lands amid a broader uptick in digital-health investment. Companies in the sector raised $7.4 billion in the first half of 2026, up roughly $1 billion from the same period in 2025, according to Fierce Healthcare . The outlet counted 244 completed deals in that window, with $4.2 billion invested in the first quarter and $3.2 billion in the second.
A notable share of that capital came in the form of megadeals. Nineteen companies raised 20 financings of at least $100 million in the first half of 2026, representing 45 percent of all capital invested, Fierce Healthcare reported, citing deals that included AI radiology company Aidoc's $150 million raise. Clinical-reference platform OpenEvidence, a comparable player in physician-facing AI tools, announced its own $210 million Series B at a $3.5 billion valuation in mid-2025, co-led by Google Ventures and Kleiner Perkins with Sequoia Capital, Coatue, Conviction and Thrive also participating, according to a release distributed via PR Newswire . That company said it planned to use its funding to expand strategic content partnerships feeding its medical knowledge library, a goal that echoes Vumedi's own stated plans to grow its content, features and formats.
For now, Vumedi's leadership has framed the new capital as fuel for expansion rather than a pivot. The company's stated plans, per FinSMEs, center on investing in people and product to expand its AI-driven video and podcast library.

Zacua Ventures raises $135 million to invest in robotics, physical AI and industrial technology
November 15, 2026 by Sam Francis
Venture capital firm Zacua Ventures has closed its second investment fund at $135 million, more than doubling the size of its original $56 million fund as it expands its focus on robotics, physical AI and technologies for industrial applications.
The San Francisco-based firm says Fund II was 35 percent oversubscribed, attracting commitments from more than 30 corporate and institutional investors across over 20 countries.
Originally focused on construction technology, Zacua is broadening its investment strategy to include manufacturing, energy, mining, infrastructure and other sectors it collectively describes as the “Physical Industries”.
The firm believes these sectors offer substantial opportunities for technologies that combine robotics, artificial intelligence and software with practical industrial expertise.
Vivin Hegde, founding partner at Zacua Ventures, says: “The industries that underpin modern life are entering a forced transformation cycle. Housing is out of reach. Energy grids are under pressure. Workforces are aging out. The AI infrastructure buildout is placing even greater demands on the industries already struggling to keep pace.
“These are not isolated problems; they’re converging across the Physical Industries, a category venture capital has largely overlooked. We built Zacua in construction because we saw these challenges firsthand. Fund II takes what we learned there and applies it to the broader physical world.”
Building on construction robotics investments
Zacua has already invested in 34 early-stage companies across 11 markets, with several investments demonstrating its interest in industrial automation.
Among its portfolio companies is Gravis Robotics, an ETH Zurich spinout developing physical AI for autonomous construction equipment. The company raised $200 million in Series A funding from SoftBank earlier this year, reaching a reported valuation of $1 billion.
Another investment is Origin Robotics, whose OG1 robot autonomously finishes interior walls. The company emerged from stealth with $20 million in seed and Series A financing, with Zacua leading the latter round.
Other investments include Flexnode, which develops modular data centers, and CURA Climate, which is working on technologies to reduce emissions from cement production.
Zacua’s first exit came earlier this year when construction risk-management software company Document Crunch was acquired by Trimble.
Expanding industrial investment
Fund II’s investors include Volvo Group Venture Capital, Holcim Maqer Ventures, Hilti Venture, Trimble Ventures, Acciona, DPR Construction, Mortenson and Dubai Future District Fund.
The firm says its corporate investor network provides portfolio companies with access to industrial customers, technical expertise and opportunities to test emerging technologies in operational environments.
Juan Nieto, founding partner at Zacua Ventures, says: “Fund I proved that our model works in one of the most complex and consequential industries in the world.
“Fund II allows us to take that same playbook much further. We are not changing what we do. We are applying the same early-stage conviction, founder-first philosophy and industry network across the broader Physical Industries.”
Zacua has already begun investing from Fund II, with robotics, industrial AI and infrastructure technologies expected to remain central to its strategy.

candidates.title: Co-Brand Card Platform Imprint Raises $130M at a $1.9B Valuation as AI Reshapes Commerce
candidates.snippet: Co-Brand Card Platform Imprint Raises $130M at a $1.9B Valuation as AI Reshapes Commerce Wowtale
candidates.text:
When AI shopping assistants find, compare and pay for products, brands risk losing their direct relationship with customers. McKinsey projects that agentic commerce could mediate up to $1 trillion in U.S. retail revenue by 2030. Imprint , which builds co-branded credit cards so brands can stay part of everyday spending, has raised $130 million.
Co-branded cards, built from the ground up
Imprint is a payments, loyalty and customer intelligence platform that helps brands make every transaction more valuable. Founded in 2020 and based in New York, it builds co-branded credit cards with brands and owns its stack across origination, risk, servicing and rewards. That gives brands control of their financial products and room to tailor rewards, the company says.
Since the start of the year it has launched programs with Albertsons Companies, Fanatics, Kroger and Shell, with the Fanatics card debuting this week. Booking.com is also a customer. Imprint reports more than two million members and partners whose annual U.S. consumer spending exceeds $500 billion. Total cardholder spending across its partners more than doubled between 2025 and 2026, and the share of spending on Imprint cards at partner checkouts tripled in a year. It also added $1.5 billion in warehouse capacity and priced its second AAA-rated asset-backed securitization, with demand nearly five times the offering size. These figures come from the company.
For the AI era, Imprint released a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that lets AI agents securely reach members’ rewards, virtual cards and transaction history, along with tools for members to review and authorize agent-initiated purchases. Imprint Access, launching today, gives customers who are new to credit or rebuilding it, backed by a refundable deposit, the same ongoing rewards as a brand’s unsecured card, with a path to upgrade. The Federal Reserve estimates 32 million Americans have little or no credit history.
A law graduate from Dublin who came to cards through WeWork
Founder and CEO Daragh Murphy is Irish, studied law at University College Dublin and was a vice president of operations and strategy at WeWork, according to Irish media. He founded Imprint in 2020 with Gaurav Ahuja and Michael Pechman. Ahuja, a partner at Thrive Capital , is reported to have helped incubate the company and to serve as chairman. Imprint raised a $75 million Series C at a $600 million valuation in October 2024, and press reports put its December 2025 Series D at $150 million and a $1.2 billion valuation.
Valuation up from $1.2B
Imprint said it raised $130 million at a valuation of about $1.9 billion. Existing investor Khosla Ventures led. Existing investors Hedosophia , Ribbit Capital , Spice and Thrive Capital took part, and Positive Sum joined as a new investor. The money will fund new payment options and AI capabilities, so brands can recognize and reward customers however they choose to pay. The release did not name the round.
CEO Murphy said brands that invest in understanding each customer and building individual relationships will win as every digital touchpoint becomes personalized. Patrick O’Shaughnessy, CEO and partner at Positive Sum, said AI makes every option easier to compare, so earning a customer’s preference matters more, and that the team’s full-stack technology and marquee partners gave the firm conviction. Fanatics CFO Glenn Schiffman said Imprint’s technology made it possible to design a card around fans.
Competitors
In U.S. rewards cards, Bilt Rewards is the most visible rival. It started as a card that turns rent into points and raised $250 million in July 2025 at a $10.75 billion valuation, led by General Catalyst and GID. It was reported to be ending its relationship with Wells Fargo and moving its cards to Cardless. No new round since 2026 could be confirmed.
Large issuers that have long run retailer co-brand programs, such as Synchrony and Bread Financial , compete for the same brands. Imprint pitches its own technology stack as the edge in designing products. Among companies we have covered, Ramp approaches cards through corporate spend management and raised $1.85 billion at a $60 billion valuation last month.

candidates.text:
Adaspace Technology raised HK$750 million ($95.6 million) in a Hong Kong initial public offering, and its shares moved higher by the midday break after opening below the offer price. The debut puts a listed supplier of AI-powered satellites and satellite-data services on the market as the company seeks funding for research, production and facilities.
Reuters reported that the shares opened at HK$24.44, 1.8% below the HK$24.90 offer price, and were last at HK$24.60 in its morning report. Bamboo Works later reported a rise to HK$25.26 by the midday break, 1.45% above the offer price. Those are snapshots from different points in Friday’s session; neither is a closing price.
The Chengdu-based company sold 30.12 million shares at HK$24.90 each, the bottom of its marketed range of HK$24.90 to HK$33.20, Reuters reported. The wire also said the retail tranche was subscribed 3.43 times and the international offering was covered 1.79 times. Those figures describe separate parts of the offering and should not be combined as one subscription measure.
Reuters describes Adaspace as a maker of AI-powered satellites that also provides satellite-data services. The Hong Kong exchange’s November 12 global-offering announcement identifies Adaspace Technology and refers investors to the company’s November 5 prospectus. The filing is the primary record for the offering; Reuters and Bamboo Works provide independent reports on the first trading session.
Bamboo Works reported net proceeds of HK$652 million ($83.6 million). It said the company plans to use 35.6% of that amount to strengthen research and development, 24.4% to build a center in Shenzhen, 20% for strategic investments and acquisitions, and 10% to repay bank loans. These are the allocations listed in the report; they do not account for every part of the proceeds.
The same report gave a snapshot of the company’s recent finances. Adaspace recorded first-half 2026 revenue of 226 million yuan ($33.9 million), down 6.3% from a year earlier. Its net loss narrowed 21.5% to 150 million yuan. The revenue decline and narrower loss are separate measures, so the loss reduction does not mean revenue grew.
For the Adaspace Hong Kong IPO, the distinction between the amount raised and the net proceeds matters: Reuters reported the HK$750 million raise, while Bamboo Works cited HK$652 million in net proceeds. The reports also show a share price that first fell below the offer price and later moved above it by midday, without establishing the final close.
The debut marks the start of public trading for the company’s shares, while the planned research, production and Shenzhen spending remain future uses of the funds. The available reports do not establish how quickly those investments will translate into additional satellites, data services or revenue. They document the offering terms, early trading and the company’s stated financial results, leaving later operating performance to subsequent disclosures.

British Business Bank: Additional £40 Million Commitment Supports Harwood Fund
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 1:09 PM
British Business Bank: Additional £40 Million Commitment Supports Harwood Fund
The British Business Bank has committed an additional £40 million to Harwood Private Capital to increase the availability of flexible financing for smaller and lower-middle-market businesses across the United Kingdom.
The investment supports the first closing of Harwood Private Capital UK Fund II. Commitments to the fund and its related co-investment vehicles now total approximately £120 million.
Harwood will use the capital to provide debt financing for privately held companies pursuing organic expansion, acquisitions, and shareholder transitions. The strategy gives business owners an alternative to conventional bank lending or a complete sale through an M&A transaction.
The commitment increases the British Business Bank’s total investment with Harwood to £75 million. The government-owned development bank previously committed £35 million to the manager’s inaugural HPC UK SME Fund in 2020.
Harwood specializes in flexible private-credit solutions for lower-middle-market companies. Its target borrowers include founder- and family-owned businesses that need additional growth capital but want to preserve ownership and strategic control.
The inaugural fund invested across digital technology, clean-energy supply chains, manufacturing, tourism, and other sectors. One portfolio example is Western Marinas, a Welsh marina operator that used Harwood financing to restore facilities in Wales and southwest England.
That investment supported local jobs and family-operated businesses while attracting visitors and economic activity to surrounding coastal communities. It demonstrates how private credit can finance physical assets and regional companies that may not fit the standardized requirements of traditional lenders.
The British Business Bank’s mandate is to improve access to capital for smaller companies and address financing gaps that can limit growth, productivity, and job creation. In its 2025-2026 financial year, the bank supported £9.4 billion of financing for approximately 38,000 businesses.
That total included £1.3 billion of public funding, £4.3 billion of private capital attracted through the bank’s programs, and £3.7 billion of guaranteed lending. Around 30,000 recipients had not previously received support through the institution.
Harwood Private Capital UK Fund II is intended to extend this impact by supplying customized debt structures for companies whose requirements may not be served adequately by banks or private equity investors.
KEY QUOTES:
“Many smaller businesses continue to face challenges accessing the flexible growth capital they need to scale, invest and realise their ambitions. Harwood has developed a strong track record of providing tailored financing solutions to UK SMEs, particularly those that have not been backed by private equity. Our commitment will help increase the availability of growth capital for businesses, support economic growth and create jobs throughout the UK.”
Adam Kelly, Managing Director of Debt and Regional Funds at the British Business Bank
“The British Business Bank has backed Harwood Private Capital since our first fund, and this renewed commitment reflects the strength of that partnership. Founder and family-owned businesses are the backbone of the UK economy, yet many are still underserved by traditional lenders whilst wishing to maintain ownership control. The £120m of committed capital allows us to keep providing the flexible, partnership capital these businesses need to grow, make acquisitions and manage ownership transitions on their own terms.”
Haseeb Aziz, Managing Partner at Harwood Private Capital

By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:56 AM
Orakl Oncology: $34 Million Series A Funding Co-Led By Norrsken VC And Singular To Expand AI-Powered Cancer Drug Discovery
Orakl Oncology, an artificial intelligence-driven biotechnology company developing technologies to improve the prediction of cancer drug responses, has raised $34 million in Series A funding co-led by Norrsken VC and Singular. The financing will support the company’s continued expansion, international hospital partnerships, and development of its AI platform, which combines patient-derived tumor samples, clinical information, and experimental biological data to advance oncology drug research.
The financing was announced by Diane-Laure Pagès, Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer of Orakl Oncology, who highlighted the company’s growing network of cancer research partners and expansion plans. The company was founded in 2023 by Pagès, Fanny Jaulin, Ph.D., and Gustave Ronteix.
Orakl originated at Gustave Roussy, the French cancer research and treatment institution where Pagès completed her doctoral studies.
Since its founding, the company has expanded from three co-founders to a team of more than 40 scientists, engineers, AI researchers, and business professionals.
Approximately 30% of its employees hold doctoral degrees.
Orakl plans to establish additional teams in the United States and United Kingdom as it expands its international research and commercial operations.
Building AI Models Around Patient-Derived Cancer Biology
Orakl Oncology is developing an AI platform designed to improve the predictability of responses to cancer treatments.
A central component of its strategy involves generating and analyzing biological information derived from patient tumors.
Cancer treatment responses can vary significantly between patients, even when they have cancers classified within the same disease category.
These differences create challenges for pharmaceutical researchers seeking to identify which experimental medicines are most likely to demonstrate beneficial effects.
Orakl is addressing this problem by combining AI with experimentally generated biological data and associated clinical information.
The company believes training AI systems on information closely connected to actual patient biology can support more relevant drug development research.
Its technology is intended to help researchers understand relationships between tumor characteristics and responses to potential treatments.
Rather than relying exclusively on publicly available datasets, Orakl is building proprietary biological information through its research infrastructure and hospital collaborations.
This approach is designed to provide a foundation for developing AI models focused on oncology drug response prediction.
Expanding International Hospital Partnerships
Orakl has established a network of hospital partnerships supporting access to patient tumor samples and related clinical information.
The company signed five hospital partnerships during 2026.
It also expects more than 15 additional cancer centers across Europe, North America, and Asia to join its network.
These relationships are an important component of Orakl’s approach to developing its AI platform.
Participating hospitals provide research-ready tumor samples and clinical information that can be analyzed alongside laboratory-generated data.
The company says its research infrastructure can generate up to 200 gigabytes of information per patient across seven matched data modalities.
Combining multiple types of biological and clinical information can help researchers investigate relationships that may not be apparent from individual datasets.
Orakl believes its international hospital network provides access to a broader range of cancer biology and research material.
The company also sees the combination of hospital relationships, laboratory infrastructure, proprietary datasets, and AI technology as an important differentiator.
Combining Laboratory Research And Artificial Intelligence
Orakl’s platform brings together experimental biology and computational analysis.
Laboratory research provides biological observations that can be used to investigate how tumors respond to different treatment approaches.
AI systems can analyze information from these experiments alongside associated clinical and patient-derived data.
The objective is to identify patterns that could help researchers better understand drug responses and prioritize further investigation.
This approach may be useful in earlier stages of oncology drug development, when researchers are evaluating potential treatments and identifying promising therapeutic candidates.
However, Orakl’s technology remains focused on drug development research rather than providing individualized clinical treatment recommendations.
In a response to a question on LinkedIn, Pagès clarified that the company’s technology is not yet ready to be used in the clinic for individual patients.
She indicated that its current applications are focused on earlier stages of drug development.
That distinction is important because research tools designed to improve drug discovery require additional validation before they can be used to guide individual patient care.
Growing From Three Founders To More Than 40 Employees
Orakl has expanded its organization significantly since launching in 2023.
The company began with three co-founders and now employs more than 40 people across scientific and business functions.
Its workforce includes biologists, software engineers, AI researchers, and other specialists.
Approximately 30% of employees have Ph.D. qualifications, reflecting the company’s emphasis on scientific research.

candidates.snippet: Zus Health Raises $33M to Make Healthcare More Connected MedCity News
candidates.text:
Zus Health, a healthcare technology platform, announced on Tuesday that it raised $33 million in Series B funding.
Zus Health combines fragmented clinical information from EHR networks, pharmacies, laboratories and other healthcare sources into a unified, continuously updated patient record. Its platform uses AI to generate patient summaries and help clinicians access relevant health information. Its customers and partners include organizations such as Homeward Health and Circadian Health.
“The story of electronic medical records doesn’t end with the silos we have today,” said Jonathan Bush, founder and CEO of Zus Health. “We’ve spent decades digitizing healthcare, but the information still doesn’t move with the patient. We’re building a networked medical record that changes that — connecting information across the healthcare system and making it available to the people and applications that need it.”

Griffin: $20 Million Series B Funding Led By Octagon Partners To Expand Card Issuing And Stablecoin Banking Services
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 8:49 AM
Griffin: $20 Million Series B Funding Led By Octagon Partners To Expand Card Issuing And Stablecoin Banking Services
Griffin, a United Kingdom-based licensed bank providing embedded banking infrastructure to fintech companies and technology platforms, has raised $20 million in Series B funding led by Octagon Partners. Notion Capital, A+ Ventures, Nordic Ninja, Breega, and other existing investors participated in the round, which values Griffin at more than $100 million.
The financing will support the expansion of Griffin’s banking platform into card issuing and stablecoin-related services while providing capital for continued growth toward profitability.
Griffin operates a regulated banking infrastructure platform that enables businesses to integrate accounts, payments, and compliance capabilities into their products.
The company serves more than 80 businesses, including Uber, Countingup, Anna Money, Yonder, and Prosper.
Its infrastructure supports more than 300,000 underlying retail and business customers and processes nearly 10 million payments annually.
The latest investment comes approximately two years after Griffin began operating as a fully licensed UK bank.
Expanding Into Debit And Credit Card Issuing
Griffin plans to use the Series B financing to introduce card issuing capabilities.
The initial offering will enable customers to launch branded retail and corporate debit cards using Griffin’s banking infrastructure.
This will extend the company’s existing services beyond accounts and payments.
Businesses using Griffin’s platform will be able to combine banking accounts, payment processing, and card products through a single infrastructure provider.
The company also intends to introduce credit card capabilities following the initial debit card launch.
These services are designed for fintech businesses and other technology companies that want to offer financial products without independently developing every component of the underlying banking infrastructure.
Griffin believes adding cards will strengthen its relationships with existing customers while creating opportunities to serve additional businesses.
The expanded platform will provide more options for companies developing financial services embedded within their own applications.
Developing Stablecoin Payment Infrastructure
The second major area of investment involves stablecoin-related banking services.
Griffin plans to develop reserve capabilities for businesses operating in the stablecoin market.
The company also intends to integrate on-chain cross-border payments into its platform.
Stablecoins are digital assets designed to maintain a relatively stable value, often by referencing a conventional currency.
Businesses developing stablecoin-based financial services may require banking relationships, reserve management arrangements, and payment infrastructure.
Griffin’s planned capabilities are intended to support these requirements.
The company’s existing regulated banking operations provide a foundation for developing additional services.
The stablecoin initiatives remain planned product developments rather than capabilities that the announcement identifies as fully launched.
More Than 80 Companies Use Griffin’s Infrastructure
Griffin has expanded its customer base since becoming a fully licensed bank in 2024.
The company initially worked with five businesses testing its systems.
Its platform now supports more than 80 companies offering financial products and services.
These customers include established businesses and fintech platforms across different financial services categories.
Griffin provides clearing and embedded banking capabilities, allowing customers to deliver banking products under their own brands.
The company currently serves more than 300,000 underlying retail and business customers.
Its infrastructure processes nearly 10 million payments each year.
The expansion illustrates increasing adoption of Griffin’s model of combining regulated banking services with technology infrastructure designed for other businesses.
Recurring Revenue Grows 3.2 Times Year Over Year
Griffin reported that recurring revenue increased 3.2 times year over year for its financial year ended September 2026.
The figures are based on unaudited financial accounts and remain subject to change following completion of the company’s statutory audit.
The company was also included in the Sifted 250 ranking of Europe’s fastest-growing startups by revenue.
Additionally, Griffin joined Tech Nation’s Future Fifty 2026 cohort, which recognizes high-growth UK technology businesses.
Octagon Partners highlighted the company’s commercial development and its progress toward achieving double-digit millions of pounds in annual recurring revenue.
The investor also emphasized Griffin’s combination of proprietary technology, AI, and regulated banking infrastructure.
The company operates under the supervision of the Prudential Regulation Authority and Financial Conduct Authority.
Supporting Fintechs Through A Regulated Banking Platform
Griffin’s business model combines banking authorization with technology services designed for fintech companies and platforms.
The company offers services including business accounts, embedded accounts, payments, safeguarding, and compliance-related infrastructure.
These capabilities allow customers to develop financial products while relying on Griffin for regulated banking functions.
Its strategy emphasizes providing a unified infrastructure platform that can support different financial services applications.
By adding card issuing and stablecoin capabilities, Griffin intends to broaden the range of products its customers can offer.
The company also believes the expanded platform will improve its ability to attract additional fintech partners.

Pune Startup Froncort.AI Gets $2.3 Mn Google.org Grant For AI Disease Screening App
Froncort.AI, a Pune-based healthcare AI startup, has received a $2.3 million grant from Google.org to build a mobile tool that tells frontline health workers which households to screen first for tuberculosis and other infections.
The grant comes with $200,000 in Google Cloud credits and pro bono engineering support. It is Google.org’s second grant to the company, after funding a validation study of its AI-NETRA platform in 2025.
How the Company Was Selected
Froncort.AI is one of 15 organisations worldwide picked for the Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation, a $30 million programme whose recipients were announced on 15 September.
Read More: Sachin Tendulkar Backs Waste Management Startup Recykal
Funding Confido Health Raises $12.5 Million To Automate Healthcare Administration With AI Funding Prodoc AI Raises Seed Funding From Dr A. Velumani Family Office
Google.org said winners were chosen from more than 2,600 proposals. Froncort.AI is one of four recipients in the health category, alongside Flexbone, Helium Health Foundation and the University of Warwick.
Read More: How to Choose the Best Travel Agency in Jaipur for a Memorable Rajasthan Holiday
That ratio explains why the grant matters more than its size. Being selected from 2,600 applicants is third-party validation that a health ministry or a state programme can cite.
What mAI-NETRA Does
The grant funds mAI-NETRA, a mobile version of the company’s public health platform.
Froncort.AI’s system combines government health programme data with satellite-derived insights from Google’s Earth AI models. It also weighs local indicators such as settlement density, land use, rainfall and flood exposure.
From that, it flags higher-risk areas within 300-metre zones and turns them into ranked work plans, household clusters and routes that health workers can follow on field visits.
The Froncort.AI app works offline with automatic sync and offers multilingual voice guidance. Matters in districts where connectivity is patchy.
Why Routing Beats Testing Alone
India’s tuberculosis programme already has tests, drugs and reporting systems. What it lacks is a way to decide where to spend a health worker’s day.
Sending a worker street by street in a high-burden district is expensive and random. Sending the same worker to a ranked cluster of households with recent flooding and dense housing is a different use of the same salary.
Froncort.AI already has TB and malaria modules are already in place. The platform is being built to cover six diseases: TB, leprosy, malaria, dengue, cholera and leptospirosis.
What the Founder Says
“The world does not lack experts. It lacks their reach,” said Ujjwal Rao, founder and chief executive of Froncort.AI. He described AI-NETRA as putting that expertise in the health worker’s hands at the door, showing where to go, whom to screen and when.
India’s health system already collects enormous amounts of data through national programmes. The gap is turning that data into a route a health worker can follow on a Tuesday morning.
Satellite inputs add something the health records cannot: environmental risk. Flood exposure and land use predict leptospirosis and vector-borne outbreaks before a single case is reported.
Froncort.AI’s constraint is field support. A model that guides screening only helps if district officers trust it and if ASHA workers can use it on low-end phones.
The programme is a useful test of whether philanthropy can fund public health AI at the pilot stage, where venture capital rarely goes.
What to Watch
Three things will decide whether this scales. The first is state adoption, because a central pilot that never reaches district workflows changes nothing.
The second is field accuracy. A routing model that sends workers to the wrong households wastes the scarcest resource in the system. Is their time.
The third is data integration. The platform is only as good as the government datasets it can legally and technically connect to. That varies by state.

Google: Gemini 4 Hydrogen Launches With Faster Agentic AI, 1 Million-Token Context Window, And New Multi-Model Orchestration
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 7:36 AM
Google: Gemini 4 Hydrogen Launches With Faster Agentic AI, 1 Million-Token Context Window, And New Multi-Model Orchestration
Google has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new artificial intelligence model designed to deliver faster execution, improved reasoning, and greater efficiency across software development, enterprise workflows, and everyday AI applications. The model features a 1 million-token context window, four adjustable reasoning levels, and expanded capabilities for autonomous AI agents, while Google is also introducing a multi-model orchestration system that coordinates different Gemini models within a single workflow.
Announced on November 12, 2026, Gemini 4 Hydrogen joins Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon models, which are designed for more demanding reasoning tasks.
While Carbon and Argon focus on complex problems requiring deeper analysis, Hydrogen emphasizes rapid execution across coding, research, data analysis, and other agentic workflows.
Google is making Hydrogen available across Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, Google Search, and Google Antigravity for eligible paid subscribers.
The company has priced Hydrogen at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, with flat pricing across its entire 1 million-token context window.
Google says Hydrogen achieves a score of 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high reasoning setting, compared with 50 for Gemini 4 Argon. Hydrogen reaches 54 at its highest reasoning setting, known as xhigh.
New Orchestrator Coordinates Multiple Gemini Models
One of the most significant additions accompanying Hydrogen is Orchestrator, a new capability within Google Antigravity that dynamically switches between AI models during a single development session.
The technology is designed to use different models for different stages of a task rather than relying on one model throughout an entire workflow.
For example, Gemini 4 Carbon can handle complex architectural decisions or coordinate a development project, while Hydrogen performs code generation, testing, debugging, and verification.
Google says this approach allows developers to combine the reasoning capabilities of its frontier models with Hydrogen’s execution efficiency.
In Terminal-Bench 4.0 testing, Orchestrator achieved task success rates approaching those of Carbon while consuming an average of 24% less quota and completing tasks 19% faster.
The system also supports parallel AI agents operating across isolated workspaces.
These agents can work simultaneously on different parts of a software development project, potentially reducing execution time and resource consumption.
Google believes this multi-model approach can help organizations optimize AI workloads based on task complexity, latency requirements, and operating costs.
Major Improvements Over Gemini 3.8 Flash
Hydrogen represents a significant upgrade over Google’s previous Gemini 3.8 Flash model.
At its default high reasoning setting, Hydrogen completes tasks approximately 2.5 times faster while improving its Terminal-Bench 4.1 score from 18.2% to 57%, according to Google’s evaluations.
The company also reported that Hydrogen reduces fabricated claims by more than fivefold compared with Gemini 3.8 Flash.
The new model is designed to respond more effectively when tools fail, searches return no results, or workflows encounter unexpected obstacles.
For software development, Hydrogen supports repository analysis, issue resolution, debugging, code generation, and iterative testing.
Google says the model can identify and repair problems while limiting unnecessary modifications to unrelated parts of a codebase.
Its ability to perform multiple file-reading and search operations in parallel is intended to improve efficiency when working with large software repositories.
In early partner evaluations involving complex graphs, SQL, and data-intensive enterprise applications, Hydrogen completed tasks between two and 2.8 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash while reducing token usage by 12% to 23%.
Performance Across Agentic AI And Professional Workflows
Google reported improvements across benchmarks measuring autonomous execution, technical reasoning, and professional knowledge work.
Hydrogen ranks fifth on Agent Arena, a live benchmark assessing AI agents performing open-ended tasks.
On HLE-Diamond, a benchmark measuring advanced domain reasoning, the model achieved a score of 58.8%.
Hydrogen also achieved 52.3% on Vals Tax Agent Bench, ranking first overall, and 55.8% on Vals Legal Research Bench, tying for first place.
Google reported that the model leads its class on AutomationBench-AA, which evaluates agentic automation capabilities.
These results reflect Google’s efforts to position Hydrogen for enterprise applications requiring both technical reasoning and reliable execution.
Potential use cases include software engineering, business research, financial analysis, legal research, and workflows involving multiple connected applications.
1 Million-Token Input And Output Capabilities
Hydrogen supports a native 1 million-token input context window and up to 1 million output tokens.
These capabilities are intended to help the model process large volumes of information and produce extensive structured results.
Google says Hydrogen can analyze complex PDFs, spreadsheets, charts, audio, and recorded video while generating reports and other deliverables grounded in source materials.
On the Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark, Hydrogen achieved a score of 53.4%, outperforming other evaluated models on end-to-end tasks involving complex visual files.
The model also scored 71.6% on Agents’ Last Exam version 1.1, a benchmark focused on professional workflows.
